title: SCOS 2000 and FIRST/PLANCK
status_notes: Minutes dated 20 April 2000 of the meeting dated 19 April 2000 at ESOC H-I (form header, PDF p. 1). Open action items for J-F. Kaufeler are marked 'AI' (PDF p. 4).
summary:
Minutes (reference TOS-OF/2000/318/SJD/HS, dated 20 April 2000) of the meeting at ESOC between ESA and the FIRST and Planck instrument principal-investigator (PI) groups. The subject was adopting [SCOS-2000](../scos2000/index.md) for instrument EGSE and real-time assessment (RTA). ESOC was represented by J F Kaufeler, J Dodsworth and N Peccia, and ESTEC by B E Melton, J Riedinger and P Estaria. The other participants came from TESRE/CNR, OAT, MPE, RAL, LAL, LABEN, IAS, SRON and KUL.

The minutes follow the agenda. C Mazza (Head of TOS-G) stated that ESA/TOS would support SCOS 2000 for both flight operations and EGSE development. P Estaria confirmed SCOS 2000 as the baseline for MOC operations. ESOC reported that the Solaris COTS set would also be available on Linux and that ObjectStore would probably be replaced. B Melton's PROBA account covers several points. SCOS 2 was the basis of the system, and its ORACLE database was extended to the SCOE equipment. A Delphi-based router carries a TM processor that extracts virtual channels or packets from transfer frames. The TC COP protocol runs in the router through a COTS product. Messages to and from the SCOEs are routed by APID, using APIDs outside the spacecraft range. Test procedures were written in Tcl/Tk.

The minutes go on to record licence and service terms (help desk included in a 35 KEURO/year/user service price), the handling of the PIs' Delta URD (ESOC keeps one product line; changes are funded as ESA infrastructure or by the customer) and the PIs' need for a core option by May 2001 for DPU testing. All PI groups unanimously stated their intention to use SCOS 2000 as the basis for EGSE and RTA. Companions: the [agenda](scos2000-meeting-agenda-2000.md), the [slides](tos-gc-first-planck-presentation-2000.md) and the [licence note](spire-sw-licence-application.md); see [SCOS-2000 as EGSE](../scos2000/egse.md).

contents.title: Welcome by C Mazza (Head of TOS-G)

key_points.text: C Mazza: SCOS 2000 is a stable, mature, reliable product, and ESA/TOS will support it for both flight operations and EGSE development.
The baseline for MOC operations is SCOS 2000; ESOC was to ask for a comment in the ITT that SCOS 2000 is the baseline for the core of the Flight Control System.
ESOC confirmed that the COTS set available for Solaris would be available on Linux (Windows NT under investigation) and that ObjectStore would probably be replaced by a cheaper object database.
PROBA EGSE: SCOS 2 was the basis; its ORACLE database was extended to the SCOE equipment, addressed like a spacecraft subsystem; the router is Delphi based.
The PROBA TM processor takes transfer frames and extracts virtual channels or packets for onward routing; TM throughput depends on packet size, number of VCs and DMA characteristics.
The TC COP protocol is built into the PROBA router using a COTS product from De Lande Long; this is probably not needed for an instrument SCOE.
The test procedure environment (TPE) accesses the ORACLE database directly at compilation time; messages to SCOEs are routed by APID, using APIDs outside the spacecraft range.
A common project database is to be provided by the Prime; ESOC's options were ORACLE, MS Access or custom solutions, and the MS-Access-based Integral database tool is compatible with SCOS 2000.
A first-level help desk is included in the service option price of 35 KEURO/year/user.
ESOC keeps one SCOS 2000 product line; changes are either infrastructure enhancements (ESA funded) or project-specific (customer funded), possibly delivered as add-ons.
The PIs need a core option by May 2001 to support DPU testing; the three FIRST instruments agreed a common EGSE development with requirements frozen about June 2000.
The interface with FINDAS will use DDS in the mission; the ESOC infrastructure would be ready between the end of 2001 and mid 2002.
Conclusion: all PI groups unanimously stated their intention to use SCOS 2000 as a basis for EGSE and RTA, to be reflected in the ITT documentation (IID).

notes: The bilingual (English/French) form labels in the header use a symbol font whose text layer is shifted by 29 code points ('PHHWLQJGDWH' = 'meeting date', 'VXEMHFWREMHW' = 'subject/objet'). The footer address is garbled the same way; it has been decoded for this entry. The Greek capital delta of 'Δ-URD' extracts as '<'. The header gives the meeting date as 19 April 2000, but the agenda (scos2000-meeting-agenda-2000) covers 18-19 April, and the minutes note '19/04/2000 resumption at point 8 of the Agenda' (PDF p. 3). The conclusion has a typo, 'SCOS 200'. No author is printed; 'SJD/HS' in the reference are initials. The participant list on PDF p. 5 gives e-mail addresses, which are omitted here. The text extraction has a trailing empty page 6.
